{"filepath":"ssd_definitions.md","content":"The most common expansion of "SSD" is "Solid‑State Drive".

1. Solid‑State Drive (SSD)
- Definition: A non‑volatile data storage device that uses semiconductor flash memory (no moving parts) to store persistent data.
- Typical domain/context: Computing / storage hardware
- Citation: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solid-state_drive

2. Social Security Disability (SSD)
- Definition: A U.S. federal program (often shortened to SSD or SSDI for Social Security Disability Insurance) that provides benefits to people who are unable to work because of a qualifying disability.
- Typical domain/context: Social services / government benefits / law
- Citation: https://www.ssa.gov/disability

3. Sum of Squared Deviations / Sum of Squares (SSD)
- Definition: In statistics, the sum of squared differences between observed values and a reference (mean or model), used to quantify variance or model error.
- Typical domain/context: Statistics / data analysis
- Citation: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSD_(disambiguation)

4. Single‑Shot Detector (SSD)
- Definition: A real‑time object detection algorithm (Single Shot MultiBox Detector) that predicts object bounding boxes and classes in a single pass.
- Typical domain/context: Machine learning / computer vision
- Citation: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SSD_(disambiguation)

(Note: "SSD" has many other domain‑specific meanings; the list above gives the top commonly encountered expansions with Solid‑State Drive as the most frequent.)"}
